text.p: Italian bond futures slumped by late afternoon well over a full point as investors worried about possible delays to Europe's single currency with most other European bond markets tumbling as well.

Dealers said added worries over how the Italian government was going to keep its finances in order to meet the criteria for EMU as opposition over its planned 1997 mini-budget seemed to be growing, keep keen buying interest to a minimum.
"It's a sellers market out there and support levels are simply not holding, the sentiment appears very negative across Europe at the moment," said one LIFFE trader.

The lira sensing the difficulties fell against the German mark breaching the 1,000 lire/mark level. Dealers said that the Bank of Italy was keeping a close but discreet watch as the lira tested support around the day's lows at 1,003 lire/mark.

Talk that EMU might be delayed grew on Monday after German finance minister Theo Waigel's weekend remarks that fulfilling the criteria for European Economic and Monetary Union was more important than sticking to a strict timetable.
"Clearly, Italy faces a touch confidence test by the financial markets on its ability to get its finances in order," said the LIFFE trader.
Dealers pointed out that BTPs and the lira had both sensed the problems with EMU and Italy's ability to get its finances in order for convergence with its northern European neighbours.
"These worries are not going to go away quickly and we see further falls in BTPs his week," said another LIFFE trader.
